name: Immersion Science Program (Fox Chase Cancer Center)
what_you_do: Take an 11 week laboratory research training course on Saturdays at Fox Chase (about 30 lab hours), then present your results on week 11. The program says it is nearly all cost free for students.
who_can_apply: Students at least 16 years old who finished both high school biology and chemistry. Neither can be taken at the same time. Open to students in the Philadelphia Tri-State area. You can apply to a Philadelphia-only section.
pay_detail: Nearly all programming is cost free to participants. No pay for the winter course. Fox Chase cannot provide transportation.
duration: 11 weeks of Saturday sessions from early January to mid March: Section 1 meets 8:30 to 11:30 a.m. and Section 2 meets 12:30 to 3:30 p.m. There are 16 seats, 8 per section.
deadline_text: The application launches in mid to late October each year and stays open about 3.5 weeks. The exact 2026 dates are not posted on the page read. Interviews are in early to mid December and letters go out by email before December 31.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Google form application. It cannot be saved, so a PDF version is available to draft offline. Two letters of recommendation are required. One must come from a science or STEM teacher who has known you at least a year. Applications are blind reviewed. Then three committee members interview 20 to 25 applicants.
notes: The FAQ says the application launches in mid to late October, so it may open any day now. Check the page for the real dates. General Fox Chase number: 888-369-2427. A summer fellows track is funded by National Cancer Institute grants. Its pay and rules are not stated on the pages read.
